title: AEZS / AF / AFC / AFCE — Ticker Reuse, Security Identity, Turnaround Timing and Value Crystallization V9

notes: AF is a historical ticker-reuse collision: 2004 and 2006 ideas are Astoria Financial; 2009 and 2014 ideas are AlarmForce Industries. The SQL companies table maps AF only to AlarmForce and therefore mislabels the older two ideas.
AFC is another ticker-reuse collision: the 2002 idea is Allmerica Financial common equity; the 2008 idea is Allied Capital 6.875% senior unsecured notes due 2047.
Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: AF 2004, AF 2014, AFC 2002, AFCE 2007, AFCE 2011.
AF 2006 is genuinely an Astoria Financial Short.
Allied Capital AFC 2008 is a debt-security idea, not common equity.
No source-DB horizon performance rows were found for these ten ideas. Corporate actions, SEC-reported operating results and direct consideration are therefore the primary outcome anchors.
AFCE 2004 included a $12/share special cash dividend, so raw stock-price charts would materially understate total shareholder payoff.
AEZS experienced an unusual path: Macrilen's confirmatory trial initially missed its objective, but FDA approval followed in December 2017; Zoptrex failed Phase III.
AlarmForce 2009's 200k-250k subscriber target was not met; subscriber count was 144.2k in 2015, but BCE later acquired the company for C$16/share.
AFCE 2011 entry around $14.65 ultimately crystallized at RBI's $79/share cash acquisition in 2017.

batch_lessons: Historical ticker symbols are not stable entity identifiers; date, legal entity and security type must be part of the canonical key.
The same AF ticker represented Astoria Financial and later AlarmForce Industries, while AFC represented Allmerica common and Allied Capital debt.
Bank EPS bridges should model asset yields, funding costs, deposit beta, prepayments and curve shape jointly rather than add isolated savings linearly.
Subscription unit economics can remain attractive while geographic growth forecasts fail because CAC and churn vary by market.
A hated insurance run-off segment can create upside when the market assigns negative value but restructuring releases capital.
Distressed debt can be an excellent investment even when the issuer's common equity is risky; seniority and asset coverage determine payoff.
Special dividends require total-return reconstruction; raw stock-price charts are misleading.
Turnaround direction and turnaround timing are separate variables.
A company can migrate from asset-sale special situation to turnaround to compounder; each stage requires a different underwriting framework.
Corporate actions such as divestitures, debt redemption and cash acquisitions are strong external value-validation anchors.
